meta_description: Australian passport photos must be 35–40 mm wide, 45–50 mm high, with a 32–36 mm face on a plain white or light grey background. Check every rule, then crop yours free.
h1: Australian Passport Photo Size and Requirements
subtitle: Crop your photo to 35 × 45 mm and print a sheet, checked against the Australian Passport Office guidelines.

requirements.notes_h3: Common reasons Australian photos are rejected

rows.label: Photo size
rows.value: 35–40 mm wide × 45–50 mm high (this tool uses 35 × 45 mm)

rows.label: Background
rows.value: Plain white or light grey, contrasting with your face

rows.label: Printing
rows.value: Colour dye-sublimation print (not inkjet) on glossy paper of at least 200 gsm

rows.label: Glasses
rows.value: Not allowed unless you cannot remove them for medical reasons. Poor eyesight alone is not a reason.

rows.label: Expression
rows.value: Face the camera, eyes open, neutral expression (children under 3 may have their mouth open)

rows.label: Head coverings
rows.value: Religious coverings only. They must be plain with no pattern and show your whole face from chin to forehead, including the edges.

notes: Inkjet or home prints. The Passport Office requires dye-sublimation prints on heavy glossy paper, so take the PDF sheet to a photo lab or kiosk that prints this way.
Retouching of any kind, including smoothing skin or removing moles, wrinkles or scars.
Hair covering the edges of your face, shadows, reflections, or a tilted head.
Wireless earbuds. Hearing aids are allowed, but AirPods and similar must come out.
Jewellery or piercings that cover part of the face or reflect light.

The Passport Office recommends a professional photo provider and warns against online photo services and apps. Use this tool to check your framing, and make sure the final print meets every rule above.
requirements.checked: Checked against these sources in November 2026. Rules change, so confirm on the official page before you apply.

how_to.title: How to make a Australian passport photo
how_to.step1_text: Stand in front of a plain background in even light and have someone else take the photo at eye level. Follow the Australian rules below.
how_to.step2_text: Choose the photo. It is processed in your browser and never uploaded to a server.
how_to.step3_text: Drag the frame to centre your face and use Zoom until your head fills the frame to the size the rules require.
how_to.step4_text: Download the PDF sheet and print it at actual size (100%, no "fit to page") on photo paper, then cut out the photos.

items.q: What size is an Australian passport photo?
items.a: Between 35 and 40 mm wide and 45 to 50 mm high, with your face measuring 32–36 mm from chin to crown. A standard 35 × 45 mm photo fits the range.

items.q: Can I wear glasses in my Australian passport photo?
items.a: No, unless you cannot remove them for medical reasons. In that case the frames must not cover your eyes and there must be no reflection on the lenses. Vision impairment alone is not accepted.

items.q: Can I print my Australian passport photo at home?
items.a: Not on an inkjet printer. Photos must be colour dye-sublimation prints on glossy paper of at least 200 gsm. Print the PDF sheet at a photo lab that uses dye-sublimation printers.

items.q: How old can my photo be?
What if a medical condition stops me meeting the rules?
items.a: Provide a medical certificate or complete a B-11 form explaining why.
